name: Xapian
tagline: Mature C++ probabilistic full-text search library with bindings for a dozen languages.
description: Xapian is an open-source C++ library for adding full-text search to applications. It ranks results with probabilistic models such as BM25, and supports phrase and proximity queries, boolean filters, stemming in many languages, spelling correction, synonyms, faceting, relevance feedback and geospatial filtering, with on-disk databases that can be searched together or remotely. It grew out of the Muscat engine and first shipped as Xapian 0.5.0 in 2002; Omega, a bundled search application, handles indexing documents and websites. Release 2.1.0 (August 2026) is current, with 1.4.x still maintained. It suits teams that want an embeddable library rather than a search server.

scale.notes: Shard by splitting into multiple databases and searching them together, locally or via the remote backend.

strengths: Embeddable library: no JVM or separate server to operate
High-quality ranking (BM25 and other models) with stemming for many languages
Bindings for a dozen languages and decades of production use
Actively released, with a long-supported stable branch
weaknesses: GPL licence complicates embedding in proprietary software
No built-in clustering, REST API or analytics features of Elasticsearch-style servers
Smaller ecosystem and fewer tutorials than Lucene-based tools
useCases: Search inside desktop and server applications
Indexing documentation, mail archives or websites with Omega
Search in Python, Perl or PHP apps without running a search server
notIdealFor: Log analytics and aggregations at scale
